bio:
Andrew G. Pringle was born about 1836, probably in Plymouth Township, Luzerne County, Pennsylvania, the son of James Pringle, a farmer, and Elizabeth Croup, and a grandson of Samuel and Martha (Lamoreaux) Pringle. The meaning of his middle initial is unknown. In 1850, aged 14, he was at home with his parents and with Alby, Noah, Leva Ann and Edwin; the widow Hulda Pringle and her children lived two doors away. His descent is the link through which his son Addison Pringle, and John's family after him, descends from the Croup and Lamoreaux lines, the route by which the family's Revolutionary ancestry is proved.

In 1857 he married Catherine Scott of Kingston. In 1860 he was a laborer of 24 living in Plymouth with Catharine, 23, and their daughter Ellen, 2, next door to his parents. By 1870 he owned $500 in real estate, and the household had grown to Ellen Jane, 12, John, 8, Samuel, 7, Addison, 5, Orange, 3, and a four-month-old girl, Julia, probably named Julia Ann after Catherine's mother; his father James, 71, widowed or separated, was living with them. In 1880 he was still a laborer, with Katharine, 43, John, 20, Samuel, 17, Addison, 15, also a laborer, Orange, 13, a slate picker, and Stella, 5; a 15-year-old servant next door, Emma Pringle, was a relative of unknown connection. In naming sons Orange and Samuel he followed the old Lamoreaux and Pringle pattern.

The marriage ended in divorce. Catherine brought the action, which the court sustained; the grounds are not known. By 1900 she described herself as divorced, and by 1910 as a widow, so Andrew had died by then; family records put his death in 1900 in Luzerne County. Their seven children were Ellen Jane, John, Samuel, Addison, Orange, Julia and Stella, five of whom were living in 1900.

researchNotes:
Andrew G. Pringle was born about 1836, probably in Plymouth Twp: he was 14 in the 1850 census (enumerated 14 Sep 1850) and 44 on 4 Jun 1880. The tree shows him as 1835-1900 (transcription: c1836-1900). The 1850 census of Plymouth Twp (A. Atherton, Ass't Marshal, page 140/141, stamp 71; dwelling 944/family 964) lists James Pringle 51 farmer ($500 real estate, b. PA), Elizabeth 48, Alby 27, Noah 16 farmer, Andrew 14 (line 38), Leva Ann 11 and Edwin 9. Two households earlier (dwelling 942) was the widow Hulda Pringle with children Orange, Ransom and 'Caturah'. The census states no relationships, but Noah is documented as son of James and Elizabeth (Croup) Pringle and grandson of Samuel and Martha (Lamoreaux), so Andrew's parentage is settled; John found this page himself on FamilySearch, attached to Andrew Pringle 1836-1900 (KG4S-XMF). He married Catherine Scott of Kingston in 1857; they had seven children per Bradsby. She later sued for divorce, 'the action commenced by her and sustained by the court'; no grounds are stated anywhere online. In the 1880 census (Plymouth Twp, ED 145, p.4) he was a laborer, with Katharine 43, John 20, Samuel 17, 'Adason' 15 (laborer), Orange 13 (slate picker) and Stella 5; next door was a 15-year-old servant, Emma Pringle, a relative of unknown connection. He named sons Orange and Samuel, following the Lamoreaux/Pringle naming pattern. He died in 1900 (tree; no record found). No Civil War, GAR, pension, will (not in the Luzerne wills index 'P') or occupation record was found online; he is not in the 2,656 Bates-transcribed PA company rosters on PA-Roots.

Two census sheets attached to Andrew's FamilySearch profile close the gap between the 14-year-old of 1850 and the married man of 1880. On 7 August 1860 Andrew Pringle, 24, laborer, was living in Plymouth with Catharine, 23, and daughter Ellen, 2, in the dwelling immediately after that of James Pringle, 61, farmer, and Elizabeth, 57, with Edwin, 18 - the same James, Elizabeth and Edwin of the 1850 household ([R4-S1]). This places Andrew, as an adult with Catherine Scott, next door to his parents, which is the documentary step an SAR/DAR application needs between the 1850 household and the 1880 family. On 29 July 1870 (indexed as 'Prindle') Andrew, 36, laborer, owned $500 in real estate; the household was Catharine 34, Ellen Jane 12, John 8, Samuel 7, Adison 5, Orange 3, an infant girl 'Julian' aged 4/12 (probably Julia Ann, named for Catherine's mother Julia Ann Scott) and James, 71 - evidently Andrew's widowed or separated father ([R4-S2]).

The infant Julia(n) explains Catherine's later counts: she reported 7 children born and 5 living in 1900, when she was listed as divorced ([R4-S3]), and 11 born/5 living as a widow in 1910 ([R4-S4]). Ellen Jane, John, Samuel, Addison, Orange, Julia and Stella make seven; the two 'Ellen' and two 'Stella' profiles on FamilySearch are probably duplicates rather than extra children. Catherine's 1910 entry as 'widowed' supports Andrew's death before April 1910, consistent with the tree's 1900; in June 1900 she called herself divorced, which does not tell us whether he was then alive.
